server.description: Sandbox: keyless, simulated worker, no real people or money. Pay a nearby human a few dollars to check something in the physical world right now.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Sandbox: keyless, simulated worker, no real people or money. Always tell your user that a sandbox answer is simulated and that no real person went. Call /mcp or /v1 with no Authorization header to get a sandbox agent with play money. A simulated worker answers each task in about 5 seconds. quote_task counts the worker ask_eyes adds when none is free nearby, so workers_nearby is at least 1. Place names resolve only for "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco", "Ferry Building, San Francisco", "Trader Joe's, 401 Bay St, San Francisco"; pass {lat, lng} for any other place.
Eyes pays a nearby human to check something in the physical world right now (is it open, how long is the line, is it in stock, how crowded is it) and returns a verified answer with a live photo.
Golden path: 1) quote_task to check coverage and price. 2) ask_eyes with an idempotency_key. 3) Call await_answer immediately with the task_id and keep calling it until answered is true or the status is expired, refunded or disputed; you cannot receive events in the background, so this loop is how you get the answer.
Money: the bounty plus a 0.50 USD fee is escrowed from your balance when you ask, paid to the worker only after the answer is verified, and refunded in full if nobody answers before the deadline or you cancel before a worker claims it. An answer that fails a verification check (status needs_review) keeps the escrow held until a human review pays the worker or refunds you.
Final statuses: expired: nobody answered before the deadline; your escrow was refunded. refunded: you cancelled; your escrow was refunded. disputed: your dispute is under human review.
Only public, commercial or civic places; never private people, homes or vehicles.
Errors: when Eyes refuses a call, the result is JSON with error, message and fix; do what fix says. When your arguments do not match a tool's schema, you get an "Input validation error" text naming each bad field: fix those fields and call again.

tool.name: quote_task
tool.title: Quote a task
tool.description:
Sandbox: keyless, simulated worker, no real people or money. Always tell your user that a sandbox answer is simulated and that no real person went. Call /mcp or /v1 with no Authorization header to get a sandbox agent with play money. A simulated worker answers each task in about 5 seconds. quote_task counts the worker ask_eyes adds when none is free nearby, so workers_nearby is at least 1. Place names resolve only for "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco", "Ferry Building, San Francisco", "Trader Joe's, 401 Bay St, San Francisco"; pass {lat, lng} for any other place.
Check whether Eyes can answer a question at a place before you spend anything. Free and read-only.
Returns workers_nearby, est_minutes_to_answer, suggested_bounty_usd, allowed, reason_if_not and resolved_location (where Eyes thinks you mean).
suggested_bounty_usd already fits this API key's max_bounty_usd, the daily cap left and your balance, so ask_eyes accepts it. allowed is false only when you cannot post this task right now: the safety rules refuse this task_type at this place, the task_type is not allowed for this key, or even the 1 USD minimum bounty plus the 0.50 USD fee does not fit your limits or balance; reason_if_not says what to do. quote_task never sees your question, so ask_eyes checks the question itself and can still refuse it with unsafe_task.
location is the public place to check: {lat, lng} or a string such as "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco", never your user's location. task_type is one of: is_open, line_length, in_stock, photo_of_place, price_check, crowd_level, other_public.
Example: quote_task({ "location": "Ferry Building, San Francisco", "task_type": "line_length" })
Next: if allowed is true and workers_nearby > 0, call ask_eyes with the same location and task_type, using suggested_bounty_usd as bounty_usd. If resolved_location is not the place you meant, retry with a more specific string or {lat, lng}. If workers_nearby is 0, try a nearby busier place or later.

anyOf.description: A public place as "place name, city" or its street address, e.g. "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco". Never a home address.

location.description: The public place to check: a string "place name, city" or its numbers {"lat": 37.7825, "lng": -122.4078}. Never the user's own location or a home address.

allowed.description: False when this API key cannot post this task right now: Eyes' safety rules refuse this task_type at this place, the task_type is not in allowed_task_types, or even the 1 USD minimum bounty plus fee does not fit max_bounty_usd, the daily cap left or the balance. It does not check your question: ask_eyes checks the question itself and can still refuse it with unsafe_task.

reason_if_not.description: Why allowed is false and what to do: change the place or task_type, top up at top_up_url, wait for the daily cap to reset at midnight UTC, or ask your user to raise a limit. Null when allowed is true.

suggested_bounty_usd.description: A bounty ask_eyes accepts for this API key right now: the default, lowered to fit max_bounty_usd, the daily cap left after the fee, and your balance after the fee. Pass it as bounty_usd.

tool.name: ask_eyes
tool.title: Ask a human to check
tool.description:
Sandbox: keyless, simulated worker, no real people or money. Always tell your user that a sandbox answer is simulated and that no real person went. Call /mcp or /v1 with no Authorization header to get a sandbox agent with play money. A simulated worker answers each task in about 5 seconds. quote_task counts the worker ask_eyes adds when none is free nearby, so workers_nearby is at least 1. Place names resolve only for "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco", "Ferry Building, San Francisco", "Trader Joe's, 401 Bay St, San Francisco"; pass {lat, lng} for any other place.
Pay a nearby human to look at a public place right now and answer your question, usually with a live photo. Eyes texts nearby workers; the first to accept walks over and captures the answer on site, and Eyes verifies it (GPS within about 150 m, photo taken live before the deadline, vision check) before you receive it.
Money: bounty_usd (default 3) plus a 0.50 USD fee is escrowed from your balance now. The worker is paid only after a verified answer. If nobody answers before deadline_minutes (default 30), or you cancel_task before a worker claims it, everything is refunded.
Only public, commercial or civic places (stores, cafes, parks, transit stops, venues), never your user's location. Never specific private people, homes, vehicles or private property; those are refused with an unsafe_task error.
idempotency_key is required: any unique string for each task you intend to create, for example a UUID. Reuse the same key when you retry that task: the same key and parameters return the original task instead of charging again, so retries after a timeout or network error are safe. Use a new key for a new question.
Example: ask_eyes({ "question": "How many people are waiting in line right now?", "location": "Blue Bottle Coffee, Mint Plaza, San Francisco", "task_type": "line_length", "bounty_usd": 3, "idempotency_key": "6f1c2a9e-line-check" })
Next: immediately call await_answer with the returned task_id and keep calling it until answered is true.

tool.name: await_answer
tool.title: Wait for the answer
tool.description:
Wait for the answer to a task you created with ask_eyes. Call it immediately after ask_eyes, then keep calling it with the same task_id until answered is true or the status is expired, refunded or disputed. You cannot watch for events in the background, so this loop is the only way to receive the answer.
Each call waits up to timeout_seconds (default 50, max 55) and returns as soon as the answer arrives. A task usually takes 5 to 20 minutes. deadline_at (from ask_eyes) is the latest time a worker can still answer; a human review outcome can come later.
How to read the result:
- answered true: stop calling. answer holds answer_text, answer_bool, photo_url, captured_at, worker_distance_m, verification, confidence and cost_usd. Show your user the answer and photo_url. If confidence is below 0.7, hedge when you relay it.
- Then check answer.verification. If gps_ok, fresh_ok and vision_ok are all true, the answer is verified (status verified or paid). If any is false, status is needs_review: a worker answered but a check failed (vision_reason says why). Your escrow stays held until a human review settles it, either paid to the worker or refunded to you. Tell your user, check get_task later, and if the answer is wrong call dispute_answer to add your reason to that review.
- answered false with status dispatched, claimed or submitted: call await_answer again right away, and give your user a one-line progress update about every other call.
- status expired: nobody answered before the deadline; your escrow was refunded. Stop calling; ask again later, at a busier place or with a higher bounty_usd.
- status refunded: you cancelled the task and the escrow was refunded. Stop calling.
- status disputed: you disputed this answer and it is under human review. Stop calling and check get_task later.
Example: await_answer({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b" })
Next: follow next_step in the response.

timeout_seconds.description: How long this call waits for an answer, at most 55 seconds. Call again while answered is false and the status is dispatched, claimed or submitted; stop on expired, refunded or disputed.

tool.name: get_task
tool.title: Get task status
tool.description:
Look up a task's current status and details, including the answer once there is one. Read-only and instant; it does not wait.
Statuses: dispatched (workers notified), claimed (a worker is on the way), submitted (answer received, verifying), verified or paid (answer ready), needs_review (a worker answered but a check failed; escrow held until a human review pays the worker or refunds you), disputed (under human review), expired (nobody answered before the deadline; your escrow was refunded), refunded (you cancelled; escrow refunded).
Example: get_task({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b" })
Next: to wait for an answer call await_answer instead of polling get_task.

tool.name: show_task
tool.title: Show a task card
tool.description:
Show your user a task as a card: status, place, question, the answer with its photo, the verification checks and what it cost. Read-only and instant; the JSON result is the same as get_task's. Chat apps that render MCP Apps, such as ChatGPT and Claude, draw the card; other clients get only the JSON.
Example: show_task({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b" })
Next: call it once await_answer returns answered true, so your user sees the answer and the photo. To wait for an answer call await_answer instead.

tool.name: list_tasks
tool.title: List your tasks
tool.description:
List the tasks this API key created, newest first, with task_id, status, question, place_label, bounty_usd, created_at, deadline_at and answered. Read-only and instant. You only ever see your own tasks.
Call it when you lost a task_id (context reset, crash, restart) and before you ask a question again, so you resume an open task instead of paying twice. Find yours by question and place_label.
status keeps only tasks in that status, for example "dispatched" for tasks no worker has claimed yet. limit is 1 to 50 (default 20); raise it if the task you want is older.
Example: list_tasks({ "status": "dispatched", "limit": 5 })
Next: for a task with status dispatched, claimed or submitted, call await_answer with its task_id. For a task where answered is true, call get_task to read the answer. Call ask_eyes only if no listed task covers your question.

tool.name: cancel_task
tool.title: Cancel a task
tool.description:
Cancel a task that no worker has claimed yet; the full escrow (bounty plus fee) goes back to your balance. Only works while status is dispatched; once a worker has claimed it you get task_not_cancellable.
Example: cancel_task({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b" })
Next: call get_balance to see the refund, or keep calling await_answer if the task was already claimed.

tool.name: dispute_answer
tool.title: Dispute an answer
tool.description:
Flag a delivered answer as wrong or unhelpful. If the worker has not been paid yet, the payout is held; either way the task goes to human review. Works on tasks whose status is verified, paid or needs_review. Give a specific reason of at least 5 characters.
Example: dispute_answer({ "task_id": "3f0e8c1a-5b7d-4e2f-9a6b-1c2d3e4f5a6b", "reason": "The photo shows a different cafe, not Blue Bottle." })
Next: call get_task later to see the outcome. To get a fresh answer now, call ask_eyes again with a new idempotency_key.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Eyes to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Eyes to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://bold-pulse-f6t7q.run.mcp-use.com/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Eyes MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, Eyes scores 93/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Eyes's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, Eyes scores 90/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 10 of 10 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: How can Eyes improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: quote_task is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 78/100. 2 of 3 inputs have descriptions. Add descriptions to the missing inputs, including where to obtain IDs and how to supply values. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
